problem: Which of the following gives the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=2{x}^{2}$ along the quarter-circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4,$ traversed from the point $(-2,0)$ to the point $(0,-2)$ in the third quadrant?

activity_context.topic_title: Line Integrals of Scalar Functions Over Circles

feedback.problem: Which of the following gives the line integral of the function $f(x,y)=y\,\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}$ along the quarter-circle ${x}^{2}+{y}^{2}=4,$ traversed from the point $(0,2)$ to the point $(-2,0)$ in the second quadrant?
feedback.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}f(x,y)\,\text{d}s={\int }_{a}^{b}f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t.
$$

 

The curve $C$ is a part-circle of radius $2$ centered at $O,$ shown below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14066920/assets/d0ae53dd5d0932cbf834a166e851c227f75cb546b591a9fd43930ec06f0e9ddf.png)

The curve $C$ can be parametrized as 

$$
r(t)=⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩,\,\frac{\pi }{2}\le t\le \pi .
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get following:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)j \\  & =-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+2\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j \\ ‖{r}^{′}(t)‖ & =\sqrt{{(\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t})}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡t)^{2}+(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t+4{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =\sqrt{4({sin}^{2}⁡t+{cos}^{2}⁡t)} \\  & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since $f(x,y)=y\,\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}},$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t)) & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\sqrt{4-(2\operatorname{cos}⁡t)^{2}} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\sqrt{4-4{cos}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =2\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,\sqrt{4{sin}^{2}⁡t} \\  & =4{sin}^{2}⁡t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}y\,\sqrt{4-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}s & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }f(r(t))\,‖{r}^{′}(t)‖\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }4{sin}^{2}⁡t\cdot 2\cdot \text{d}t \\  & =8{\int }_{\pi /2}^{\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡t\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$
